## Overview
The Library Management System is a cloud-native platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It is deployed strictly within EU data centers to meet data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patron**: End-user accessing self-service portals.
- **Librarian / Staff**: Internal user managing cataloging and circulation.
- **Library Management System**: Core platform comprising Web Frontend, API Gateway, and Core Services.
- **Web Frontend**: React and TypeScript Single-Page Application.
- **API Gateway**: Spring Cloud Gateway.
- **Core Services**: Domain-driven Spring Boot microservices (Catalog, Circulation, User Management).
- **Primary Database**: PostgreSQL 16 with PgBouncer.
- **Search Index**: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch cluster.
- **Cache Layer**: Redis in-memory data store.
- **Message Broker**: Apache Kafka.
- **External Systems**: Stripe EU (Payment Gateway), SendGrid EU (Notification Service), EU Identity Provider (OIDC/Keycloak/Auth0), National Library Registry, and Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network.

## Relationships
- **Patron / Librarian -> Web Frontend**: Accesses UI via HTTPS/TLS 1.3.
- **Web Frontend -> API Gateway**: Routes requests via HTTPS.
- **API Gateway -> Core Services**: Forwards internal requests via REST/gRPC.
- **Core Services -> Primary Database**: Persists relational data via JDBC/TCP.
- **Core Services -> Search Index**: Queries catalog metadata via REST/TCP.
- **Core Services -> Cache Layer**: Reads/writes hot-spot data via RESP/TCP.
- **Core Services -> Message Broker**: Publishes asynchronous events via Kafka protocol.
- **Library Management System -> External Systems**: Integrates with Stripe (REST/HTTPS), SendGrid (REST/HTTPS), National Registry (OAI-PMH), IdP (OIDC/HTTPS), and ILL Network (ISO 18626/HTTPS).

## Technology Stack
- **Java 21 & Spring Boot**: Core language and framework for robust backend microservices.
- **React & TypeScript**: Modern frontend technology for responsive patron and staff UIs.
- **PostgreSQL 16**: Relational storage ensuring ACID compliance for circulation data.
- **Elasticsearch / OpenSearch**: Dedicated search cluster meeting the <800ms 99th-percentile search performance requirement.
- **Redis**: Low-latency caching for sessions and frequent catalog reads.
- **Apache Kafka**: Asynchronous event-driven decoupling for notifications and audit logs.

## Rationale
The microservices architecture with a dedicated search index and cache layer ensures high performance, meeting the strict search latency requirement. Strictly pinning all cloud components, databases, and third-party SaaS integrations to EU regions satisfies the mandatory data residency constraint.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive digital solution designed for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. The architecture prioritizes strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance.

## Key Elements
- Library Patron and Librarian / Staff (Users)
- Web Application Container (React/TypeScript via Nginx)
- API Gateway Container (Kong/Envoy)
- Core Services Container (Java/Spring Boot)
- Search Service Container (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch)
- Database Container (PostgreSQL EU region)
- Redis Cache Container
- Background Worker Container (Python/Celery)
- Event Broker Container (Apache Kafka EU-hosted)
- Digital Asset Storage Container (MinIO / S3-compatible Object Storage, EU-hosted)
- External Systems: Stripe EU, SendGrid EU, EU Identity Provider, National Library Registry, Interlibrary Loan Network

## Relationships
- Web App to API Gateway: HTTPS/REST and WebSockets
- API Gateway to internal containers: gRPC for low-latency communication
- Core Services to Search Service: Apache Kafka TCP protocol over TLS (event-driven index updates)
- Core Services to PostgreSQL: SQL over TCP (EU-bound)
- Core Services to Redis Cache: RESP over TCP
- Core Services to Event Broker: Kafka Protocol over TLS
- Core Services to Background Worker: AMQP via RabbitMQ
- Core Services to Digital Asset Storage: HTTPS/REST (S3 API) with pre-signed URLs
- External integrations (Stripe EU, SendGrid EU, EU IdP, National Library Registry, ILL): HTTPS/REST

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript & Nginx: Frontend Single Page Application
- Kong/Envoy: Edge routing, SSL termination, and JWT auth validation
- Java/Spring Boot: Core business logic container for cataloguing and circulation
- OpenSearch: Dedicated search index ensuring R-05 sub-800ms performance
- PostgreSQL: Primary transactional store with strict EU data residency enforcement
- Redis: In-memory cache for catalogue metadata acceleration
- Apache Kafka: Event streaming platform with TLS for decoupled, asynchronous messaging
- MinIO / S3-compatible Object Storage: EU-hosted binary storage for digital assets (PDFs, e-books)

## Rationale
This container architecture uses dedicated search and caching services to reliably achieve the 99th-percentile search response time under 800ms. Furthermore, it strictly enforces EU-only data residency constraints across all primary databases, event brokers, and object storage containers.

Web Application Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within an EU-only data residency constraint.
- The Web Application Container acts as the frontend Single Page Application serving both patrons and librarians.

## Key Elements
- Web Application Container (React/TypeScript, Nginx)
- Router Component (React Router)
- State Management Component (Redux Toolkit / React Query)
- API Client Component (Axios)
- UI Component Library (Tailwind CSS / Radix UI)
- Authentication & Session Component (OIDC/OAuth2 Client)
- Localization (i18n) Component
- Error Boundary & Telemetry Component
- API Gateway Container (Kong/Envoy)

## Relationships
- Library Patron & Librarian / Staff -> Web Application Container: Accesses portals and manages operations via [HTTPS/REST and WebSockets]
- Router Component -> UI Component Library: Renders views via [TypeScript/React props]
- Router Component -> Authentication & Session Component: Enforces route guards via [TypeScript callbacks]
- State Management Component -> API Client Component: Synchronizes server state via [TypeScript function calls]
- Authentication & Session Component -> API Client Component: Injects Bearer tokens via [Axios interceptors]
- API Client Component -> API Gateway Container: Forwards API requests and frames via [HTTPS/REST and WebSockets]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Core framework for component logic with type safety
- Nginx: Serves static assets locally to enforce EU data residency without external CDNs
- React Query & Redux Toolkit: Manages server-state caching and local state to meet <800ms search performance (R-05)
- Tailwind CSS & Radix UI: Provides accessible design system components
- Axios: Handles HTTP requests with automatic token refresh interceptors
- OIDC/OAuth2: Manages secure user authentication and JWT session tokens

## Rationale
- The modular component decomposition ensures a high-performance, responsive UI that easily meets the sub-800ms search response requirement.
- Local Nginx asset serving and strict routing through the API Gateway guarantee 100% compliance with EU-only data residency constraints.

API Gateway Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides item cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture enforces strict EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search latency requirements.

## Key Elements
- **API Gateway Container**: Kong Gateway handling edge routing, security, and telemetry.
- **Web Application Container**: React/TypeScript frontend served via Nginx.
- **Core Services Container**: Java/Spring Boot application managing business logic.
- **Search Service Container**: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for catalog discovery.
- **Database & Cache Containers**: PostgreSQL (EU region) and Redis.
- **Internal API Gateway Components**: Routing & Proxy Engine, Auth Plugin, Rate Limiting Plugin, Request Transformation Plugin, Telemetry & Tracing Component, IP Geolocation & Geo-Fencing Plugin.

## Relationships
- **Web Application Container -> API Gateway Container**: Routes frontend traffic [HTTPS/REST and WebSockets].
- **API Gateway Container -> Core Services Container**: Forwards validated requests [gRPC].
- **API Gateway Container -> Search Service Container**: Routes catalogue search queries directly [gRPC/HTTP].
- **API Gateway Container -> Redis Cache Container**: Performs rate-limiting and JWT checks [Redis RESP protocol].
- **API Gateway Container -> EU Identity Provider**: Validates OAuth2/OIDC tokens [HTTPS/OIDC].

## Technology Stack
- **Kong Gateway**: Selected for rich ecosystem of plugins (JWT, Rate Limiting, Geo-IP, OpenTelemetry).
- **OpenTelemetry (OTel)**: Used for distributed tracing to monitor P99 search latency (< 800 ms SLA).
- **Redis**: Provides fast distributed rate-limiting and JWT revocation checks within the EU cluster.
- **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch**: Delivers high-performance catalogue search bypassing core services.

## Rationale
This architecture uses an API Gateway pattern with direct search routing and edge-level security plugins to meet strict P99 latency SLAs (< 800 ms). Deploying all components within EU-hosted infrastructure strictly enforces regional data residency constraints.

Core Services Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals while strictly enforcing EU data residency. The architecture leverages a modular Java/Spring Boot core services container backed by cloud-native infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- **Core Services Container**: Java / Spring Boot container housing domain logic.
- **CatalogueComponent**: Spring Data JPA component managing physical and digital items (R-01).
- **CirculationComponent**: Component handling lending and circulation workflows.
- **SearchSyncComponent**: Spring Event Listener synchronizing search indexes.
- **CacheManagerComponent**: Spring Data Redis component for metadata caching.
- **DigitalAssetComponent**: Component managing digital asset references and storage URLs.
- **IdentityAdapter**: Spring Security OAuth2 Client for JWT validation.
- **PaymentAdapter**: Spring Cloud OpenFeign adapter for Stripe EU.
- **NotificationAdapter**: Adapter for SendGrid EU notifications.
- **IllNetworkAdapter**: Spring RestClient for Interlibrary Loan Network.
- **Apache Kafka EU-hosted**: Central event broker replacing RabbitMQ.
- **Database Container**: PostgreSQL EU region.
- **Search Service Container**: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch.
- **Redis Cache Container**: Redis caching layer.

## Relationships
- `API Gateway Container` -> `IdentityAdapter`: Forwards requests with bearer tokens [gRPC]
- `API Gateway Container` -> `CatalogueComponent`: Forwards validated requests [gRPC]
- `CatalogueComponent` -> `Database Container`: Executes queries [SQL over TCP]
- `CatalogueComponent` -> `CacheManagerComponent`: Reads/writes cache [RESP over TCP]
- `CacheManagerComponent` -> `Redis Cache Container`: Executes caching commands [RESP over TCP]
- `SearchSyncComponent` -> `Search Service Container`: Updates indexes [HTTP/REST over TLS]
- `CatalogueComponent` -> `Event Broker Container`: Publishes domain events [Kafka Protocol over TLS]
- `DigitalAssetComponent` -> `Digital Asset Storage Container`: Requests pre-signed URLs [HTTPS/REST S3 API]
- `PaymentAdapter` -> `Stripe EU`: Processes fines [HTTPS/REST]
- `NotificationAdapter` -> `SendGrid EU`: Sends alerts [HTTPS/REST]
- `CirculationComponent` -> `IllNetworkAdapter`: Coordinates loans [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- **Java / Spring Boot**: Core enterprise framework for transaction boundaries and dependency injection.
- **Spring Data JPA**: Simplifies database persistence for cataloguing and circulation.
- **Apache Kafka**: Single unified event broker and asynchronous task router (eliminating RabbitMQ to prevent sprawl).
- **PostgreSQL**: Relational database ensuring strict EU data residency.
- **Redis**: In-memory caching layer to meet sub-800ms search and retrieval performance goals (R-05).
- **Spring Cloud OpenFeign**: Declarative REST client for external service integration.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict EU data residency compliance with high performance by consolidating messaging onto Apache Kafka and utilizing Redis caching to achieve sub-800ms search responses (R-05). The modular Spring component design cleanly separates domain logic, infrastructure concerns, and external adapters for maintainability.

## Overview
The Search Service Container is a high-performance component of the Library Management System designed to handle catalogue item searches. It delivers sub-800ms 99th-percentile search responses while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
* Search API Router (FastAPI with integrated Query Sanitizer)
* Query Translator (Elasticsearch DSL / Python)
* Search Index Engine (OpenSearch with EU-only primary and replica shard placement)
* Index Synchronization Consumer (Kafka Consumer / Python)
* Redis Cache Container (System-level Redis cache for query results)

## Relationships
* API Gateway Container -> Search API Router: Forwards search queries [HTTP/JSON over TLS]
* Search API Router -> Redis Cache Container: Checks and stores frequent query results [Redis TCP over TLS]
* Search API Router -> Query Translator: Passes validated query parameters [In-process]
* Query Translator -> Search Index Engine: Executes query DSL on cache miss [REST/JSON over HTTP]
* Event Broker Container -> Index Synchronization Consumer: Streams catalog mutation events [Apache Kafka TCP over TLS]
* Index Synchronization Consumer -> Search Index Engine: Performs idempotent bulk upserts [REST/JSON over HTTP]

## Technology Stack
* FastAPI / Python: Selected for the Search API Router to provide lightweight, high-performance REST routing and middleware integration.
* OpenSearch: Chosen for the Search Index Engine under an Apache 2.0 open-source license to prevent vendor lock-in and support EU-only node deployment.
* Redis: Utilized as an external cache container to reduce query latency and protect the search engine under high load.
* Apache Kafka: Deployed for event streaming to ensure asynchronous, real-time catalogue index freshness.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves the required <800ms search performance by separating read paths through Redis caching and utilizing asynchronous Kafka-driven write ingestion. Strict EU data residency is guaranteed by restricting all OpenSearch shards and event streams exclusively to EU-hosted nodes.

- Row-Level Security (RLS): Native enforcement of EU-only data compliance
- AES-256 & LUKS: Data at rest encryption
- `pg_stat_statements`: Query optimization and performance monitoring

This component-level database architecture guarantees compliance with EU-only data residency constraints via native PostgreSQL mechanisms. Additionally, it optimizes query latency to consistently achieve the required 99th-percentile search response time under 800ms.

## Technology Stack
- Redis: In-memory database chosen for low-latency catalogue metadata acceleration
- RESP (REdis Serialization Protocol): Standardized wire protocol for Redis communication
- TLS/TCP: Encrypted transport layer ensuring strict compliance with EU-only data residency
- Redis Sentinel/Clustering: Topology management for high availability and failover

## Rationale
This component decomposition ensures predictable in-memory execution times, directly supporting the 99th-percentile search response requirement under 800 ms. Enforcing TLS and strict replication boundaries guarantees full compliance with the EU-only data residency constraint.

## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It utilizes a Python/Celery background worker container for asynchronous processing while enforcing strict EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
- **Background Worker Container (Python/Celery)**: Core container hosting asynchronous processing logic.
- **Task Router (`Task Dispatcher`)**: Routes messages from the Event Broker.
- **Notification Processor**: Handles asynchronous dispatch of emails and push alerts.
- **Catalog Synchronization Engine**: Manages batch updates to search and database containers.
- **ILL & Registry Integrator**: Executes scheduled polling with external library systems.
- **Data Purge & Archival Worker**: Executes scheduled maintenance and lifecycle tasks.
- **Task Telemetry & DLQ Handler**: Manages failed jobs, Dead Letter Queues, and Prometheus metrics.

## Relationships

Event Broker Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides item cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for academic and public libraries. It uses a decoupled event-driven architecture to meet strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Event Broker Container:** Central Apache Kafka container with KRaft-based broker storage.
- **Event Ingestion Engine:** Java/JVM Kafka broker component handling writes with EU node partition replication.
- **Topic Routing & Schema Registry:** Confluent Schema Registry enforcing Avro/JSON schemas.
- **Stream Processing / Consumer Group Manager:** Kafka Connect / KStreams managing asynchronous event consumption.
- **DLQ Manager:** Kafka Topic & Consumer Router capturing poisoned messages.
- **Broker Metrics & Health Monitor:** Prometheus JMX Exporter tracking consumer lag.
- **Access Control & mTLS Gateway:** Kafka Authorizer enforcing mutual TLS and ACLs.

## Relationships
- **Core Services Container -> Access Control & mTLS Gateway:** Authenticates and connects securely [mTLS / Kafka Protocol]
- **Access Control & mTLS Gateway -> Event Ingestion Engine:** Forwards authorized message streams [Internal TCP]
- **Event Ingestion Engine -> Topic Routing & Schema Registry:** Validates event schemas [HTTP/REST over TLS]
- **Event Ingestion Engine -> Search Service Container:** Streams change data capture [Kafka Protocol over TLS]
- **Stream Processing / Consumer Group Manager -> Background Worker Container:** Dispatches asynchronous background jobs [Kafka Protocol over TLS]
- **Stream Processing / Consumer Group Manager -> DLQ Manager:** Routes failed messages after max retry exhaustion [Internal Kafka routing]
- **DLQ Manager -> Background Worker Container:** Forwards failed events for manual inspection [Kafka Protocol over TLS]
- **Stream Processing / Consumer Group Manager -> Broker Metrics & Health Monitor:** Reports consumer lag [JMX / Prometheus scrape over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- **Apache Kafka (KRaft mode):** Provides ZooKeeper-free event broker storage within EU data boundaries.
- **Confluent Schema Registry:** Enforces strict event contract compatibility.
- **Prometheus JMX Exporter:** Monitors consumer lag to ensure <800ms search latency compliance.
- **mTLS & Kafka ACLs:** Secures inter-container transport and topic access.

## Rationale
This architecture uses KRaft-based Apache Kafka and rigorous access controls to enforce EU data residency. Dedicated streaming, monitoring, and DLQ components guarantee the high reliability and low latency required for search performance.

Digital Asset Storage Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a public and academic platform for cataloging items, managing circulation, and providing self-service portals with strict EU data residency. This architecture details the internal component decomposition of the Digital Asset Storage Container.

## Key Elements
- Object Storage Engine (MinIO Server)
- Access Control & Policy Manager
- Encryption Service
- Lifecycle & Replication Worker
- Audit & Telemetry Logger
- Core Services Container

## Relationships
- Core Services Container -> Access Control & Policy Manager: Requests pre-signed URLs and validates permissions via [HTTPS/REST (S3 API)]
- Access Control & Policy Manager -> Object Storage Engine: Dispatches authorized read/write I/O streams
- Object Storage Engine -> Encryption Service: Enforces AES-256 encryption-at-rest via [EU-hosted KMS / PKCS#11/HTTPS]
- Lifecycle & Replication Worker -> Object Storage Engine: Applies retention rules and sweeps expired objects
- Access Control & Policy Manager -> Audit & Telemetry Logger: Emits security events via [Local IPC / Syslog]
- Object Storage Engine -> Audit & Telemetry Logger: Reports metrics via [Prometheus metrics scrape]

## Technology Stack
- MinIO Go binary: Used for distributed disk persistence and erasure coding
- MinIO IAM / Open Policy Agent (OPA): Enforces bucket policies and IAM
- EU-hosted KMS (AES-256): Ensures at-rest encryption for all digital assets
- MinIO Lifecycle Management: Manages automated tiering, retention, and WORM compliance
- FluentBit / Prometheus: Captures access logs, audit trails, and performance metrics

## Rationale
This component architecture ensures secure, compliant handling of digital assets while strictly enforcing EU-only data residency constraints. It delivers robust observability, compliance features (WORM), and low-latency storage access.
